items.title: Mozambique: Govt plans 5,541 new civil service hires in 2027, with a budget impact of 1.399 billion meticais
items.summary: According to data from the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (Plano Económico e Social e Orçamento do Estado – PESOE) compiled today by Lusa, the number of new recruits projected for 2027 represents an increase of 39.9% compared with the 3,962 admissions projected for 2026, while the corresponding budget impact rises by 23.3%, from 1.135 billion meticais (€15.9 million) budgeted for this year to 1.399 billion meticais (€19.6 million) in 2027 Education will continue to account for the largest share of recruitment, with 2,978 admissions planned, equivalent to 53.7% of the total, mainly involving general education teachers. In this sector, the estimated budget impact amounts to 903 million meticais (€12.6 million), corresponding to around two-thirds of the total cost of new admissions planned for next year The proposal also provides for the recruitment of 1,364 employees for the Justice Administration bodies, more than double the 745 admissions planned for 2026.

items.title: Many feared trapped under collapsed building in Nairobi
items.summary: People are feared to be trapped after a large, unfinished building in Nairobi collapsed during construction. Rescue operations have proven complicated as police fired tear gas to disperse looters A multi-story building that was still under construction collapsed in the Kenyan capital of Nairobi on Friday, resulting in casualties and looting at the site, according to local media The Nairobi County governor's ​office confirmed the collapse, adding in a ​statement that people may be trapped beneath rubble Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building came down in a busy business-residential mixed-use district The Red Cross sent teams to the site, posting on social media: "At around 1340 hours, a multi-story building under construction collapsed on 9th Street in Eastleigh, Nairobi." There were conflicting reports on the size of the unfinished building.

items.title: Academia urged to present solutions for development challenges
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – The Minister of Agriculture, Roberto Mito, has challenged Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), Mozambique’s oldest higher education institution, to produce scientific guidance that will enable the construction of a resilient economy capable of bringing solutions to the country’s development challenges. Speaking on Thursday at the “First Symposium on Climate Adaptation and Resilience in Mozambique”, held in Maputo, the minister said that the challenge is for the entire Mozambican academic community and if “measures are implemented, they would help the nation reduce its reliance on external funding.” “Science should play a central role in identifying alternatives for national development, helping the country to leverage its existing resources and transform them into a means of financing its own priorities. Mozambique needs to rethink how it mobilizes resources for development and external funding should not come at the expense of the nation’s own capacity to find answers to its challenges.We must find local solutions to address local problems”, he said.

items.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
items.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection The first confirmed Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe International Airport, according to African health officials, as new information from Switzerland contradicts Uganda's account of the Nigerian patient's travel history Uganda , a country reporting no active Ebola infections, has become a focus of investigations into cases thousands of kilometers apart Uganda insists it has no confirmed active cases of the deadly virus .

items.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
items.summary: Watch: Trump says Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access after row Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink internet network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits had been reversed by Elon Musk who owns the satellite system The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back" Asked on Friday, Trump said: "If there is a problem, I will get it straightened out." Trump added: "I have not spoken to him. I might have to, but I have not.

items.title: Muchanga expelled from Renamo for demanding Momade’s resignation
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – Renamo party, which used to be Mozambique’s main opposition movement, has decided to expel its best known former parliamentary deputies, António Muchanga, following his suspension last February. Muchanga was one of Renamo’s main speakers in the previous parliament (2019-2024). He continues to speak regularly in television talk shows. Together with demobilized guerrillas, Muchanga has been demanding the resignation of Ossufo Momade from his post as Renamo president. For many months Momade’s opponents have been occupying Renamo offices across the country, demanding his resignation, widely blamed for Renamo’s poor showing in the October 2024 general elections. The former guerrillas also claim that they are being persecuted and even murdered by the current Renamo leadership for demanding Momade’s resignation.

items.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
items.summary: Between 150 and 200 people were in the church at the time of the shooting, according to one witness Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, officials have said At least 34 others were injured as gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing. No-one has admitted carrying out the attack In a news conference, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators which he described as a "group of extremists" Jordan's King Abdullah II, said the authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties" Initial reports indicated seven people had been killed in the attack.
